subject.title: fix(reef): bound JSONL store file reads to prevent OOM on oversized audit/replay stores

question: What recovery and retention behavior should Reef provide when an already-shipped audit or replay JSONL store exceeds the new 32 MiB safety limit?
rationale: Automatically truncating, rotating, or discarding these stores can change audit retention or replay-protection semantics, while a permanent runtime error leaves existing operators without an in-product recovery path.

options.title: Require bounded recovery before merge
options.body: Define and implement a Reef-owned retention, migration, archive, or repair path, then prove both normal operation and recovery of an existing oversized store.

options.title: Accept explicit operator recovery
options.body: Keep the hard failure only if maintainers intentionally accept manual operator intervention and document the supported recovery procedure and its data consequences.

recommendation.title: Require bounded recovery before merge
recommendation.body: Define and implement a Reef-owned retention, migration, archive, or repair path, then prove both normal operation and recovery of an existing oversized store.

likelyOwner.reason: The current patch author can apply the selected bounded implementation, but the durable data-retention choice requires broader Reef ownership confirmation.
